html:
King of Dahomey from 1818 to 1858, who took the throne in a coup with help from the Brazilian slave trader Francisco Felix de Souza.

He ended the tribute paid to Oyo in the 1820s, as Oyo collapsed, and enlarged the army of women soldiers that Europeans called the Dahomey Amazons. As Britain pressed to end the slave trade, he encouraged the export of palm oil, while still selling captives; in 1852 he signed a treaty with Britain to end the trade, which was not kept. He is remembered as one of Dahomey's greatest kings.
